claims.text: The architecture of LLM-based autonomous agents can be unified into a framework consisting of a profiling module, a memory module, a planning module, and an action module.
Agent profile generation methods in existing literature are categorized into handcrafting, LLM-generation, and dataset alignment strategies.
Memory structures in LLM-based autonomous agents are categorized into unified short-term memory systems and hybrid short-term and long-term memory systems.
Planning strategies for LLM-based agents are categorized into planning without feedback and planning with feedback from environments, humans, or internal models.
Strategies for agent capability acquisition are categorized into methods with fine-tuning and methods without fine-tuning.
Applications of LLM-based autonomous agents span social science, natural science, and engineering fields.
Evaluation strategies for LLM-based autonomous agents are categorized into subjective human-centric evaluations and objective quantitative metrics.

evidence.description: The authors propose a unified agent architecture framework composed of a profiling module, a memory module, a planning module, and an action module.
Existing literature commonly employs three profile creation strategies: handcrafting method, LLM-generation method, and dataset alignment method.
Memory structures are divided into unified memory (simulating short-term memory via in-context learning) and hybrid memory (explicitly modeling short-term and long-term memory).
Existing planning modules are organized into planning without feedback and planning with feedback, where feedback is obtained from environments, humans, or models.
Agent capability acquisition strategies are categorized into capability acquisition with fine-tuning and capability acquisition without fine-tuning.
Applications are systematically reviewed across three distinct areas: social science, natural science, and engineering.
Evaluation methodologies are reviewed focusing on subjective methods (human annotation, Turing test) and objective methods (metrics, protocols, benchmarks).

methodologies.name: Systematic Literature Survey and Taxonomy Analysis
methodologies.description: A holistic taxonomy and unified framework synthesizing existing research on the construction, application, and evaluation of large language model based autonomous agents.

limitations.text: Previous non-LLM autonomous agent research relied on simple, heuristic policy functions learned in isolated environments, diverging from human learning processes.
Existing LLM-based autonomous agents face prompt instability across interconnected modules where minor changes alter overall outcomes.
LLM-based autonomous agents suffer from slow action execution efficiency due to the autoregressive architecture of LLMs requiring multiple inference steps per action.
LLM agents are subject to hallucination during task execution and code generation, leading to false information or unexecutable actions.

future_work.text: Enhancing role-playing capability by fine-tuning models on uncommon roles and designing architectures that model human cognitive psychology.
Developing generalized human alignment mechanisms that permit agents to simulate diverse human values and negative traits for realistic social simulation.
Constructing unified and resilient prompt frameworks that maintain consistency across different LLMs and module components.
Developing methods to constrain the pre-existing web knowledge of LLMs to accurately mirror human user knowledge boundaries in simulations.
